chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'In the domestic pigeons of Mecca, excluding the pigeons of the Sanctuary, whoever slaughters a bird while he is not in a state of Ihram, upon him is to give charity; and if he is in a state of Ihram, then a sheep for each bird.'

And if he slaughters in the Sanctuary (excluding the pigeons of the Sanctuary) while he is in a state of Ihram解除 (Muhrim), upon him is its value, according to what we have previously mentioned, and he also narrated.

key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: Pigeons of the Sanctuary (specific to Mecca)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for slaughtering a bird in Mecca while in a state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general sanctity of Mecca and the specific holiness of the Haram, prescribing charity for non-Ihram individuals and a sheep per bird for those in Ihram. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the penalty for slaughtering game depends on both the location's status and the pilgrim's ritual state, reinforcing the principle of proportional expiation for transgressions within the Sanctuary.
